description: Verify entity A's visual height relative to entity B. Catches scale mismatches: tree-as-tall-as-player, house-smaller-than-character, rabbit-larger-than-human, etc.

framing.subject: both_in_frame
framing._doc: Eye-level wide shot at ~3-5m from the midpoint of A and B, pitch ~0 to slightly down. Both subjects within frame at comparable distance so pixel height is a fair proxy for world height.

prompt_template:
This capture frames two entities. Entity A ({entity_a_label}) is at world position {pos_a}. Entity B ({entity_b_label}) is at {pos_b}. Camera is at world {cam_pos}, looking-at midpoint, pitch {cam_pitch}.

In this image, is A {expected} than B? Compare PIXEL HEIGHTS of their bounding silhouettes (NOT their world Y coords — pixel height accounts for perspective foreshortening).

Answer:
  VERDICT: PASS | FAIL
  EVIDENCE: one sentence with approximate pixel-height ratio (e.g., 'A spans ~280px, B spans ~120px → A is 2.3× taller, passes "taller"').
  CONFIDENCE: high | medium | low
common_fix: Adjust state_init.scale on the wrong-sized entity. For pattern-spawned defs, check scale_min/scale_max in the pattern. If the entity is .glb-based, verify the mesh's intrinsic scale matches the def's expected world size — Tripo3D outputs are normalized to bbox=1m, so state.scale literally is meters.
